# COMMUNITY RESISTANCE GATHERING #1 HOST GUIDE

# How to Use This Document

##### Thank you for signing on to host a community resistance gathering as part of One Million Rising!

##### If you haven't already, start by taking a look at the Host Toolkit , which covers logistics and basics around scheduling and preparing for your first gathering.

##### *This guide covers what you'll do during your first gathering –the agenda, discussion* topics, and even what to say out loud.

##### We recommend following the overall content and flow of the agenda, but you may choose to make adjustments for the length of time and structure depending on the size of your group or other considerations. Additionally, the suggested wording for what to say out loud as the lead facilitator does not need to be followed exactly. It's offered as a resource for those who find it helpful, but you can choose different wording as it works for you. *Suggested wording is indicated by italics , and particularly key content ideas are indicated* by bolding .

# The Plan

### STRUCTURE AND TIMING

##### We suggest a total of 120 minutes for your gathering. Plan on about 90 minutes of content, with a cushion of about 30 minutes in case you run over or want more discussion time. This time could also flow into a potluck/meal before or after.

### GOALS

##### ● Grow community connection, resilience, and resistance ● Develop and deepen our shared understanding of…

##### ○ The moment we're in ○ The need for mass defiance ○ The "pillars" framework, and how we can influence those pillars ○ Examples of effective noncooperation tactics

##### ● Get us more ready to take action together

### WHO/HOW MANY

##### You can host a gathering as small as 2 people or as large as 40-50 (though if the number is higher, you'll want to ask friends or co-organizers to help you facilitate and host). Focus on inviting people you already know or have a connection to–or that those you're inviting have a connection to. This is also a great opportunity to invite and connect with folks in your life with whom you don't always/already talk about political issues.

### WHERE

##### You can host at home, at a public space like a library or friendly local business, or somewhere else that makes sense to you.

### WHEN

##### Ideally, this session takes place between July 31 and August 12 (between One Million Rising sessions 2 and 3) to share these ideas with others and talk about where you see opportunities for defiance in your lives.

##### Pick a second date after August 13 for your second gathering, when you'll talk about how you and your fellow gatherers will take action next–including how you can plug into national efforts!

##### Please note: Our Mobilize platform will have a cutoff of September 7 for both gatherings.

### MATERIALS NEEDED

##### Your materials and setup can be flexible to match your capacity and the size of your gathering. For instance, you could plan to have a whiteboard or flipchart for brainstorming or project the content below on a screen–or you could

### SIGN-UP

##### Our goal is to train 1 million people. In order to make sure your gathering counts towards our goal, please make sure your event is registered on Mobilize . You can then share the link with people you're inviting so they can RSVP.

### WHAT COMES NEXT?

##### Our ask for One Million Rising is that you host two gatherings: one to orient others to a strategic framework to fight authoritarianism, and another to plan how you'll take action together. The second gathering can happen after our next One Million Rising on August 13, when we'll give a full download on what campaigns and actions we can plug into right away, as well as offer guidance on how to build these actions into your second gathering.

# Full Agenda

### Part 1: Opening

#### Welcome & Joyful Opening (5 min)

##### Welcome everyone and add some context as to why folks are gathering. For example, you might say:

##### *"I'm delighted you all are here! Thank you for coming.*

##### *This is a difficult moment as we watch ICE seize people off the streets, DOGE wipe out government agencies, and so much more [ feel free to name what concerns you most ]. This gathering is a space where people can bring their joy and anger, frustration and determination, their fear and their courage, their love and their heartbreak.*

##### *Tonight we’re going to talk about where we find ourselves in this moment in time, and explore some ideas and options for what we can do about it. We’re not making any decisions and we don't have to come to any agreement. We’re exploring and supporting each other to*

ONE MILLION RISING | COMMUNITY RESISTANCE GATHERING HOST GUIDE 5

##### *make meaning of this moment. If you can come to my next gathering, we’ll go further into some specific plans. But let’s treat tonight like an orientation and a brainstorm."*

##### Then, set the tone with something that brings people into their bodies and into the room. Choose something that matches your vibe, such as:

##### ● A grounding song ● A poem of resilience ● A shared breath and intention ● An inclusive prayer or reading from a justice tradition

#### Introductions/Quick Go-Around (10 min)

##### Have each person share their name, anything they want people to know about themselves (pronoun, where they’re coming from…), and one reason they showed up today. This could be anything: why you care about this work, what you’re bringing into the space, or a personal story about the stakes in what is happening. Make it your own. Just keep it quick, no more than about a minute per person.

##### If your group is larger than 10, this will likely take more time, so you can also have people do intros in smaller groups or even pairs.

##### Remember—you’re not just building a list of names. You’re building a circle of intention.

### Part 2: Authoritarianism & Noncooperation 101

#### How are people resisting right now? (5 min)

##### Invite people to just say aloud different ways that they hear or see people resisting the Trump regime right now. Allow a free exchange of ideas and encouragement—all strategies and tactics count.

##### *As people are doing this, begin to ask “and why are people doing this?” Acknowledge there* are a wide range of reasons why people are resisting this regime.

##### *Summarize/wrap-up: “There are lots of ways people are trying to resist right now. Resistance against tyrants is beautiful. But we’ll need more than we have been doing. So there are two pieces we want to explore in this session. First is just getting clear about what*

ONE MILLION RISING | COMMUNITY RESISTANCE GATHERING HOST GUIDE 6
![image](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

##### *we’re up against. And second, exploring the concept of noncooperation—because it’s a powerful tool we need to add more to our toolbox.”*

#### Authoritarian: The wanna-be King? (10 min)

##### Introduce the concept of authoritarianism and authoritarian breakthrough.

##### *"We’re seeing dangerous consolidation of power. The basic arc of a wanna-be king is someone who wants all power flowing through them. There’s a playbook for this. We call it the Authoritarian Playbook."*

##### Direct people to look at this image on a printed piece of paper, or on a phone, tablet, laptop, or projected image.

##### Read aloud each category and invite the group to generate an example or two of each. Keep it light and moving—this doesn’t have to be a long lesson.

##### Close by saying:

##### *"Here's the thing:*

##### *1) We are in a moment of authoritarian breakthrough. This is a short window in which a would-be authoritarian regime attempts to rapidly consolidate power. This is worse than it was in the first Trump administration, and we can't wait for elections to prevent things from getting worse.*

##### *2) Donald Trump did not write the authoritarian playbook. What he does may make our democracy unsteady, but it’s not a completely new invention. Authoritarians around the world have used these tactics to try to hold onto power. Authoritarianism in the US*

ONE MILLION RISING | COMMUNITY RESISTANCE GATHERING HOST GUIDE 7
![image](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

##### *did not begin with Donald Trump, and will not end with him. But we also have a playbook for defeating it.*

##### *3) We can learn tactics and strategies from other parts of the globe who have fought and won against authoritarians. And for that, let’s explore “the pillars.”*

#### The Pillars of Support (15 min)

##### Introduce the pillars of support framework:

##### *"Every regime depends on the support of institutions: media, business, education, civil servants, faith, labor, and more.*

##### *These are the pillars holding up the system. Let me show you a picture to help think about it. These aren't all the pillars, but they'll give you the idea."*

##### Direct people to look at this image on a printed piece of paper, their handout, or on a phone, tablet, laptop, or projected image. Or you can even draw a picture of it live on a whiteboard or piece of paper.

##### *"When some of the people inside these pillars stop complying—the system wobbles. When lots of people stop complying, the system can abruptly fall. That may be needed with an entrenched autocrat.*

##### *That’s called noncooperation. Noncooperation is the act of refusing to cooperate or comply with requests, demands, or orders.*

ONE MILLION RISING | COMMUNITY RESISTANCE GATHERING HOST GUIDE 8
![image](data:image/jpeg;base64,)
![image](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

##### *Enough noncooperation will cause a pillar to be unreliable to the regime, or completely defect. Individuals, groups, pillars, and entire societies can engage in noncooperation."*

##### Give 2–3 concrete examples of compliance and defection:

##### ● Workers who refuse to unjust policies, such as the 1 million federal employees who defied orders from DOGE to send a weekly report listing “5 Things You Did This Week"

##### ● Local officials who slow-walk implementation of repressive laws, such as a New Orleans Sheriff who is rebuffing new state guidelines and continuing their policy of limited interactions with ICE

##### ● You can use the images below to help (also in the slide deck).

ONE MILLION RISING | COMMUNITY RESISTANCE GATHERING HOST GUIDE 9
![image](data:image/jpeg;base64,)
![image](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

#### Brainstorm & Discussion: Planting Seeds of Noncooperation and Courage (30 min)

##### Have people get into groups of 3-4 for focused brainstorming.

##### 15 minutes: First, take time to brainstorm and map relationships to the pillars.

##### ● What pillars am I part of? ● How are those pillars upholding the regime? ● In those pillars, what kind of defiance is already happening and what could

##### more look like? ● Who are key decision-makers in those pillars who we could influence,

##### pressure, or persuade to support more noncooperation?

ONE MILLION RISING | COMMUNITY RESISTANCE GATHERING HOST GUIDE 10

##### Return the group back together and explain:

##### *“Right now, there are already people who are taking risks in their noncooperation, like federal workers, business owners, and more. This is where resistance spreads quietly but powerfully.*

##### *I want you to do two things: 1) think of anyone in your circle who has already been risking and noncooperating and 2) think of anyone in your circle who may be given orders that they might have to defy or not cooperate with.”*

##### 10min: Send people back to groups to discuss and brainstorm:

##### ● Who do you know that’s already doing subtle or quiet defiance? ● Where could you imagine defiance in your workplace, congregation, union, or

##### school? ● Who in your life could take action if they were nudged or supported? ● Who might you have already given up on, but maybe as things deteriorate, they

##### might reconsider?

##### 5min: Now, give people a second task:

##### *“If you came up with at least one or two people, think about a plan for how you’ll reach out to them, or as many of those people as you can, to encourage them: writing a note to them, starting a conversation, or sending a message of support or encouragement. You can say, thanks for noncooperating. Or, I’ve got your back if you choose to in the future. Or, I’d be happy to talk to you in the future if you get asked to do things against your morals—we got you. This can be in any format: a letter or text message, or a direct conversation."*

### Part 3: Closing and Next Steps

#### Commitments & Next Steps (5 min)

##### Text someone from this group (or someone outside it) with a commitment for how you plan to carry this work forward. Then, make sure folks know about your next gathering. If you already have a date and time in mind, tell people and have them put it in their calendars. Or, you could offer a couple options and have people vote on the next time together, for greater buy-in.

#### Go-around closing (10 min)

##### Wrap up and invite people to share:

ONE MILLION RISING | COMMUNITY RESISTANCE GATHERING HOST GUIDE 11

##### *"Noncooperation with a wanna-be king has to be cultivated and grown. We’re planting seeds. What’s a way your courage for noncooperation is strengthened by this time together? Share in one sentence."*

##### If you have a large group, this will take more time, so you can also have people share just one word to the whole group, or share a sentence back to their small group.

#### *After your gathering*

##### A few steps will help wrap up your gathering and prepare you for what's next:

##### Please mark all attendees in your Mobilize Host Dashboard. This is an important step so we can track our progress toward our one million goal. Send us your photos of your event! Join us for One Million Rising Session 3 on August 13: register here . Reach out to everyone who came to thank them for attending and continue building your connection and solidifying their commitment. Register your second gathering on Mobilize . The goal of this gathering is to bring the Session 3 content back to your group and plan how you'll take action together. Share the link with the folks who came to your first gathering so they can RSVP and put it in their calendars. Take a breath and be proud of yourself! YOU DID IT.
